room: owner-room-01 (Owner's own bedroom, AUTH #046 internal test capture)
privacy: Metrics and text only. Video, frames, poses, splats, renders and packages stay on the box (chmod 700), the private Modal volume and the private staging bucket; nothing media-derived is in git. Deletable on request.

source_video.resolution: 1920x1080 (rotation -90: portrait for the whole clip, not mixed)

frame_selection.rule: sharpest (variance of Laplacian) per 3-frame window, very blurry windows dropped

methods: framed-shelf-photo band tracked by SIFT homography from 2 reference frames
manual boxes on shelf frames the tracker missed
masking_before_upload.verification: contact sheets reviewed; residual detector pass (YuNet + Haar frontal/profile): 79 boxes on masked frames, 30 on 29 held-out splat renders, 8 on in-engine renders, all false positives (lace, carpet, shelving, red bag); no face survives

training.recipe: quality-30k (antialiased, bilateral grid, scale reg, 30k iterations)

placement.scale_basis: assumed 2.44 m (8 ft) ceiling; ceiling plane weakly observed (59 inliers)

weak_regions.summary: Weakest: the east / south-east third (x 0.5..1.5 m, z -1.75..0.25 m: the dresser's east end and the floor between the foot of the bed and the dresser), 2.7-5.3 views with almost no view spread. The ceiling was barely filmed. Low (character-height) views are soft everywhere because every training view is from 1.3-1.7 m looking down about 60 deg.

coaching_inputs: Move slower: 14 of the 288 selection windows (0.25 s each) were too blurry to use.
Overlap more: 45 of 274 frames did not register; keep at least two-thirds overlap between consecutive views, especially when turning toward the dresser and door.
Walk a full loop around the bed and dresser (east side and the gap at the foot of the bed were seen from only 3-5 directions).
Add a low pass at knee height (30-50 cm) and a few views tilted up: the miniature character's eye is near the floor, and the ceiling sets the scale.
Keep the camera on the room, not the carpet: the last part of the clip was a long carpet-only tail.
Turn the TV off or angle away from it (reflections); lay framed photos face down or remove them before filming.
Hold the phone one way the whole time (this clip was portrait throughout, which is fine; landscape gives a wider horizontal view).
